page: Amazon Web Services r5b.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-hypervisor virtual instance engineered for enterprise data processing. The hardware foundation features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (f and vnni), AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. Backed by 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz (allocating 8.0 GB per vCPU), the instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, instead routing I/O externally with a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark analysis highlights consistent mid-tier execution across system metrics alongside specific per-core bottlenecks. The instance achieves average ratings in multi-core metrics, registering 40,671.85 on stress-ng multi-core, a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,027.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 34,689.11. Memory throughput shows an average uncached read speed of 107.9 GB/sec and a write speed of 47.88 GB/sec for 256MB blocks. In contrast, single-thread stress-ng scores (1,380.89) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.57 GB/sec) fall within the bottom 25% quartile, reflecting modest single-core throughput typical of older generation architectures.

In operational application testing, the instance exhibits solid memory and serving capabilities. It achieved 37.94 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 27.8 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound machine learning tasks demonstrate average performance on small to medium models (e.g., 58.1 prompt tokens/sec and 9.98 text generation tokens/sec on a 7B LLM), but drop to weak throughput on large 70B models (5.78 tokens/sec prompt processing). Cost efficiency is centered on high memory capacity and density rather than peak compute throughput or bundled NVMe storage. The instance fits large in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, and distributed data processing tasks requiring massive working memory.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) and 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-core execution (Geekbench multi-core score of 11,027.0 and Redis throughput of 37.94 million ops/sec), though single-thread metrics fall into lower performance quartiles. The instance prioritizes substantial RAM volume over raw single-core compute performance, making it well matched for enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory key-value stores, and distributed caching systems.
